title: First Sub-orbital Spaceflight
desc: The German V-2 rocket (MW 18014) becomes the first human-made object to cross the Kármán line into outer space.

title: First Animals in Space
desc: Fruit flies are launched aboard a US V-2 rocket to study radiation exposure, becoming the first animals in space.

title: First Primate in Space
desc: Albert II, a rhesus macaque monkey, reaches space aboard a US V-2 rocket, though he dies during impact.

title: Sputnik 1
desc: The Soviet Union launches the first artificial satellite into Earth orbit, initiating the Space Age and Space Race.

title: Sputnik 2 & Laika
desc: The Soviet Union launches the dog Laika into orbit aboard Sputnik 2, making her the first living animal to orbit Earth.

title: Explorer 1
desc: The first successful American satellite is launched, discovering the Van Allen radiation belts surrounding Earth.

title: Vanguard 1
desc: The United States launches Vanguard 1, the first solar-powered satellite, which remains the oldest human-made object in space.

title: Creation of NASA
desc: US President Dwight D. Eisenhower signs the National Aeronautics and Space Act, establishing NASA.

title: Project SCORE
desc: The world's first communications satellite is launched by the US, transmitting a Christmas message from President Eisenhower.

title: Luna 1
desc: Soviet probe becomes the first spacecraft to reach Earth escape velocity and achieve a heliocentric orbit around the Sun.

title: Vanguard 2
desc: The first dedicated weather satellite is launched by the US to measure cloud cover distribution.

title: Explorer 6
desc: The United States satellite takes the first photograph of Earth from orbit.

title: Luna 2
desc: Soviet lunar probe hits the Moon, becoming the first human-made object to impact another celestial body.

title: Luna 3
desc: Soviet probe photographs the far side of the Moon for the first time, revealing terrain drastically different from the near side.

title: TIROS-1
desc: The US launches the first fully functional television infrared observation satellite, transforming meteorology.

title: Discoverer 13
desc: The US recovers a satellite capsule from orbit for the first time, paving the way for mid-air recoveries of spy satellite film.

title: Echo 1
desc: NASA launches the first passive communications reflector satellite, a giant metalized balloon used to bounce radio signals.

title: Sputnik 5
desc: Soviet capsule carries dogs Belka and Strelka into orbit; they become the first animals to return safely to Earth.

title: Venera 1
desc: The Soviet Union launches the first planetary probe to fly past Venus, though communications fail en route.

title: Vostok 1
desc: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space, completing a single orbit of Earth.

title: Freedom 7
desc: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space, conducting a 15-minute suborbital flight under manual control.

title: Kennedy's Moon Challenge
desc: US President John F. Kennedy addresses Congress, declaring the goal of landing a man on the Moon before the decade is out.

title: First Major Orbital Breakup
desc: Transit 4A Ablestar upper stage explodes in orbit, creating ~300 trackable fragments — the first recorded accidental on-orbit fragmentation.

title: Friendship 7
desc: John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit the Earth, completing three orbits aboard a Mercury capsule.

title: Telstar 1
desc: The first active, commercial communications satellite is launched, transmitting the first live transatlantic television signals.

title: Vostok 3 & Vostok 4
desc: The Soviet Union launches the first dual human spaceflight, establishing the first multi-ship communications in orbit.

title: Mariner 2
desc: NASA probe completes the first successful planetary flyby, scanning Venus and confirming its extreme surface temperatures.

title: Vostok 6
desc: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space, orbiting Earth 48 times.

title: Syncom 2
desc: The United States launches the world's first geosynchronous communications satellite.

title: Voskhod 1
desc: The Soviet Union flies the first multi-person crew (three cosmonauts) in a single spacecraft without spacesuits.

title: Voskhod 2
desc: Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov performs the first spacewalk (EVA) in history, lasting 12 minutes outside the craft.

title: Gemini 3
desc: Gus Grissom and John Young pilot the first crewed mission of the US Gemini program, demonstrating orbital maneuvering capabilities.

title: Gemini IV
desc: Ed White performs the first American spacewalk, spending 22 minutes floating outside his spacecraft.

title: Mariner 4
desc: NASA probe performs the first successful Mars flyby, returning the first close-up pictures of a deeply cratered Martian surface.

title: Multiple US Upper Stage Breakups
desc: Peak year for orbital debris from unpassivated rocket stages. Thor-Agena and Delta upper stages explode months after launch, creating 800+ tracked fragments.

title: Gemini 6A & Gemini 7
desc: The two US spacecraft achieve the first successful active space rendezvous, maneuvering within one foot of each other.

title: Luna 9
desc: Soviet probe achieves the first survivable soft landing on the Moon, transmitting the first close-up panoramic images of the lunar surface.

title: Venera 3
desc: Soviet probe crashes into Venus, becoming the first human-made object to impact the surface of another planet.

title: Gemini 8
desc: Neil Armstrong and David Scott perform the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit with an uncrewed Agena target vehicle.

title: Luna 10
desc: Soviet robotic satellite becomes the first artificial satellite to orbit the Moon.

title: Apollo 1 Fire
desc: A cabin fire during a launchpad test kills astronauts Grissom, White, and Chaffee, forcing a major redesign of the Apollo capsule.

title: Soyuz 1 Disaster
desc: Cosmonaut Vladimir Komarov dies when his capsule parachute fails during re-entry, the first in-flight fatality of human spaceflight.

title: Cosmos 186 & Cosmos 188
desc: Two uncrewed Soviet spacecraft achieve the first fully automated docking in orbit.

title: Zond 5
desc: Soviet spacecraft carries tortoises and other organisms around the Moon and returns safely, the first life forms to circle the Moon.

title: Apollo 7
desc: The first crewed Apollo mission is successfully launched into Earth orbit, testing vital crew systems after the Apollo 1 disaster.

title: Apollo 8
desc: Astronauts Borman, Lovell, and Anders become the first humans to leave Earth orbit, travel to, and orbit the Moon.

title: Soyuz 4 & Soyuz 5
desc: Two Soviet crewed spacecraft dock in orbit, and two cosmonauts perform an EVA to transfer from one ship to another.

title: Apollo 11
desc: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin become the first humans to land and walk on the Moon, fulfilling Kennedy's goal.

title: Apollo 12
desc: Pete Conrad and Alan Bean execute a precise lunar landing, recovering parts from the robotic Surveyor 3 probe launched in 1967.

title: Apollo 13 Crisis
desc: An oxygen tank explosion cripples the spacecraft en route to the Moon, requiring a heroic emergency return effort.

title: Luna 16
desc: Soviet robotic lunar probe achieves the first automated lunar sample return to Earth.

title: Luna 17 & Lunokhod 1
desc: The Soviet Union lands the first robotic, remote-controlled space rover on another celestial body.

title: Venera 7
desc: Soviet probe becomes the first spacecraft to successfully land on Venus and transmit data back to Earth from its blazing surface.

title: Salyut 1
desc: The Soviet Union launches the world's first space station into Earth orbit.

title: Soyuz 11 Tragedy
desc: Three Soviet cosmonauts die during re-entry due to a faulty valve depressurizing the cabin after a record-breaking stay on Salyut 1.

title: Apollo 15 & Lunar Rover
desc: NASA conducts a heavy science mission to the Moon, utilizing the Lunar Roving Vehicle for the first time.

title: Mariner 9
desc: NASA probe enters orbit around Mars, becoming the first spacecraft to orbit another planet.

title: Mars 3
desc: Soviet probe achieves the first soft landing on Mars, though it transmits data for only 20 seconds before failing.

title: Pioneer 10
desc: NASA launches a probe to Jupiter, becoming the first spacecraft designed to escape the solar system and carrying the Pioneer plaque.

title: Apollo 17
desc: The final human mission to the Moon lands at Taurus-Littrow, concluding the Apollo program with record lunar stay time.

title: Skylab
desc: The United States launches its first domestic space station, utilizing the final Saturn V rocket launch.

title: Mariner 10
desc: NASA launches the first probe to use a gravitational slingshot maneuver (at Venus) to visit Mercury, imaging its cratered surface.

title: First Flyby of Mercury
desc: Mariner 10 makes its first close approach to Mercury, mapping portions of the planet for the first time.

title: Apollo-Soyuz Test Project
desc: An American Apollo capsule docks with a Soviet Soyuz capsule in orbit, marking a symbolic handshake in space and ending the Space Race.

title: Viking 1
desc: NASA spacecraft lands successfully on Mars, delivering the first long-term surface operations and life-detection experiments.

title: Voyager 2
desc: NASA launches Voyager 2 on a grand tour of the outer planets, eventually visiting Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

title: Voyager 1
desc: Launched shortly after its twin, Voyager 1 studies Jupiter and Saturn before charting a path toward interstellar space.

title: Progress 1
desc: The Soviet Union launches the first uncrewed automated cargo resupply spacecraft to the Salyut 6 space station.

title: US ASAT Program Begins
desc: The US begins testing anti-satellite weapons. In 1985, an ASM-135 ASAT missile destroys the Solwind P78-1 satellite, creating 285 trackable fragments.

title: First GPS Satellite
desc: Navstar 1 is launched, beginning the Global Positioning System constellation.

title: Voyager 1 Jupiter Flyby
desc: Voyager 1 discovers active volcanism on Jupiter's moon Io, changing human understanding of planetary geology.

title: Ariane 1
desc: The European Space Agency (ESA) conducts the successful maiden flight of the Ariane 1 launcher, establishing independent European space access.

title: STS-1 (Columbia)
desc: NASA launches the Space Shuttle Columbia, completing the maiden flight of the world's first reusable orbital spacecraft.

title: Challenger Maiden Flight
desc: Space Shuttle Challenger launches on its first mission (STS-6), featuring the first Space Shuttle spacewalk.

title: STS-7 (Sally Ride)
desc: Sally Ride becomes the first American woman in space, flying aboard the Space Shuttle Challenger.

title: First Untethered Spacewalk
desc: Bruce McCandless II uses the Manned Maneuvering Unit (MMU) backpack to float freely in space away from the Space Shuttle.

title: Giotto
desc: The European Space Agency launches Giotto to encounter Halley's Comet, later capturing close-up images of a comet's nucleus.

title: US Destroys Solwind P78-1
desc: An F-15-launched ASM-135 ASAT missile destroys the Solwind satellite at 525km, creating 285 trackable debris pieces.

title: Challenger Disaster
desc: Space Shuttle Challenger breaks apart 73 seconds into its flight (STS-51-L), killing all seven crew members.

title: Mir Space Station
desc: The Soviet Union launches the core module of Mir, the world's first modular, continuously inhabited long-term space station.

title: Buran Maiden Flight
desc: The Soviet Union launches its own reusable space shuttle, Buran, on its first and only uncrewed orbital flight.

title: Magellan
desc: NASA launches the Magellan probe from a Space Shuttle to map the surface of Venus using synthetic-aperture radar.

title: Hubble Space Telescope
desc: NASA and ESA launch the Hubble Space Telescope into orbit, revolutionizing astronomy despite an initially flawed mirror.

title: Hubble Service Mission 1
desc: Astronauts aboard Space Shuttle Endeavour install corrective optics on Hubble, fixing its blurry vision and restoring full capability.

title: Valeri Polyakov's Record
desc: Cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov returns to Earth after spending 437 consecutive days aboard Mir, setting the record for longest single human spaceflight.

title: Shuttle-Mir Program
desc: Space Shuttle Atlantis docks with the Russian station Mir for the first time, initiating cooperative US-Russian space efforts.

title: Pegasus HAPS Breakup
desc: A Pegasus rocket upper stage explodes in LEO, creating ~700 trackable debris pieces in a long-lived high-inclination orbit.

title: First Iridium Launch
desc: Five Iridium satellites launched on a Delta II, beginning the first LEO communications mega-constellation (66 satellites).

title: Mars Pathfinder
desc: NASA's lander and its tiny Sojourner rover touch down on Mars, initiating the modern era of continuous robotic Martian exploration.

title: Cassini-Huygens
desc: A joint NASA/ESA probe is launched to conduct a flagship mission to study the Saturnian system and its moons.

title: First Globalstar Launch
desc: Four Globalstar satellites launched, beginning the second LEO communications constellation.

title: ISS Zarya Launch
desc: Russia launches the Zarya module, the first component of the International Space Station, establishing a new era of global cooperation.

title: Expedition 1 to ISS
desc: Astronaut Bill Shepherd and cosmonauts Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev board the ISS, beginning continuous human occupancy of the station.

title: First Space Tourist
desc: American businessman Dennis Tito pays for a seat on a Russian Soyuz mission to the ISS, becoming the world's first self-funded space tourist.

title: Columbia Disaster
desc: Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrates upon re-entry during STS-107 due to wing damage from launch foam, killing all seven crew members.

title: Shenzhou 5
desc: Yang Liwei is launched by China, making China the third nation to achieve independent human spaceflight capability.

title: SpaceShipOne
desc: The first privately funded crewed spaceflight crosses the Kármán line, winning the Ansari X Prize.

title: Huygens Landing on Titan
desc: The ESA Huygens probe lands on Saturn's moon Titan, making the farthest landing ever accomplished on an outer solar system body.

title: New Horizons
desc: NASA launches a high-speed probe to conduct the first-ever close-up reconnaissance of Pluto and the Kuiper Belt.

title: Fengyun-1C ASAT Test
desc: China destroys its Fengyun-1C weather satellite with a kinetic kill vehicle, creating ~3,400 trackable debris pieces — the worst debris event in history.

title: Chang'e 1
desc: China launches its first lunar orbiter, beginning its long-term robotic exploration program of the Moon.

title: Chandrayaan-1
desc: India's space agency (ISRO) launches its first lunar probe, which later confirms the presence of water molecules on the Moon.

title: Cosmos-Iridium Collision
desc: Defunct Cosmos 2251 collides with active Iridium 33 at 11.7 km/s, creating ~2,000 trackable debris fragments — the first accidental hypervelocity satellite collision.

title: STS-135 (End of Shuttle)
desc: Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on the final mission of the US Space Shuttle program, concluding 30 years of operations.

title: Tiangong-1
desc: China launches its first prototype space laboratory to practice orbital docking and long-duration operations.

title: SpaceX Dragon C2+
desc: SpaceX's Dragon becomes the first commercial spacecraft to dock with and deliver cargo to the International Space Station.

title: Curiosity Rover Landing
desc: NASA's heavy Curiosity rover lands in Gale Crater using an innovative 'sky crane' system to search for past habitable environments.

title: Voyager 1 Enters Interstellar Space
desc: NASA confirms Voyager 1 has crossed the heliopause, becoming the first human-made object to enter interstellar space.

title: Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)
desc: India launches its first interplanetary mission, successfully entering Mars orbit on its first attempt in September 2014.

title: Philae Comet Landing
desc: The ESA Rosetta probe's Philae lander touches down on Comet 67P, the first soft landing on a comet nucleus in history.

title: New Horizons Pluto Flyby
desc: NASA's probe flies past Pluto, revealing a dynamic world with nitrogen glaciers, ice mountains, and a hazy atmosphere.

title: Blue Origin New Shepard Landing
desc: The New Shepard rocket executes the first successful vertical rocket landing from a suborbital spaceflight.

title: Falcon 9 First Stage Landing
desc: SpaceX successfully lands a Falcon 9 first-stage booster vertically at Cape Canaveral after an orbital launch, a milestone for reusability.

title: Falcon Heavy Maiden Flight
desc: SpaceX launches the world's most powerful operational rocket, sending Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster into a heliocentric orbit.

title: Chang'e 4 Far Side Landing
desc: China becomes the first nation to soft-land a robotic probe and rover on the far side of the Moon.

title: India ASAT Test (Mission Shakti)
desc: India destroys Microsat-R satellite in LEO, demonstrating anti-satellite capability. Most debris decays within months due to low altitude.

title: First Starlink Launch
desc: SpaceX launches 60 Starlink v0.9 satellites, beginning the largest satellite constellation in history.

title: First OneWeb Launch
desc: 34 OneWeb satellites launched from Baikonur on a Soyuz, beginning the UK-based LEO broadband constellation.

title: Crew Dragon Demo-2
desc: SpaceX launches NASA astronauts Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley to the ISS, the first orbital human launch by a private company.

title: Perseverance Rover & Ingenuity
desc: NASA lands the Perseverance rover on Mars, carrying Ingenuity, which performs the first powered controlled flight on another planet.

title: Tiangong Core Module
desc: China launches the Tianhe core module, beginning assembly of its permanent space station.

title: Russia ASAT Test
desc: Russia destroys its Cosmos 1408 satellite with a direct-ascent missile, creating 1,500+ trackable debris pieces threatening the ISS.

title: James Webb Space Telescope
desc: NASA, ESA, and CSA launch the premier infrared space observatory to observe the first galaxies and deep universe.

title: Artemis I
desc: NASA launches the uncrewed maiden flight of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft on a lunar orbit mission.

title: First Kuiper Satellites
desc: Amazon launches KuiperSat-1 and KuiperSat-2 prototypes on an Atlas V, beginning its LEO broadband constellation.

title: First SpaceSail (Qianfan) Launch
desc: China launches the first 18 Qianfan satellites on a Long March 6A, beginning its mega-constellation to rival Starlink.

title: Starlink Reaches 7,000
desc: SpaceX's Starlink constellation surpasses 7,000 active satellites in orbit, serving millions of users worldwide.

title: Kuiper Production Begins
desc: Amazon launches its first batch of production Kuiper satellites, ramping up constellation deployment.

title: Starlink Reaches 10,000
desc: SpaceX's Starlink constellation surpasses 10,000 active satellites, the first mega-constellation to reach five figures.
